_meta.indication: VELSIPITY is indicated for the treatment of moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (UC) in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled “treat-through” trial over 52 weeks with an initial 12-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.population: Adolescents aged 16 years and older and adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Coprimary endpoints: clinical remission at Week 12 and clinical remission at Week 52
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical remission at Week 12: 27.4% etrasimod vs 7.5% placebo (treatment difference 20.1%, p < 0.0001); at Week 52: 32.5% vs 6.7% (treatment difference 25.7%, p < 0.0001)

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 12-week induction trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adolescents aged 16 years and older and adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: clinical remission at Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical remission at Week 12: 26.2% etrasimod vs 15.2% placebo (treatment difference 11.2%, p = 0.010)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥5%) are headache, elevated liver tests, and dizziness. In UC-1, headache 9% vs 5% placebo, elevated liver tests 6% vs 5%, dizziness 5% vs 2%. Serious risks include infections, bradyarrhythmia and AV conduction delays, liver injury, and macular edema.
target_moa: Etrasimod is a sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator binding with high affinity to S1P receptors 1, 4, and 5; it partially and reversibly blocks lymphocyte egress from lymphoid organs, reducing circulating lymphocytes and thereby lowering activated lymphocytes in tissue.
modality: Small molecule (orally bioavailable synthetic S1P receptor modulator)

rems.type: A REMS is not considered necessary at this time.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee meeting was not held because the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected for a drug of this class.

summary.text: Standard (non-priority) NDA for a new molecular entity, reviewed and approved in the first cycle based on two adequate and well-controlled phase 3 trials; no accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designations, and no advisory committee meeting.

Application Type	NDA
Application Number(s)	216956
Priority or Standard	Standard
Submit Date(s)	October 14, 2022
The Applicant submitted the results of two adequate and well-controlled phase 3 trials (APD334-301 and APD334-302), which formed the basis of the substantial evidence of effectiveness.
Etrasimod has not been previously approved or marketed in the United States and therefore, it is classified as a New Molecular Entity (NME).

requirement.text: 4499-4 Collect data from a prospective pregnancy exposure registry, preferably a disease-based multiproduct pregnancy registry, using a cohort analysis that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to etrasimod regardless of indication during pregnancy with unexposed comparator population(s) in a timely manner.

citations.quote: 4499-4 Collect data from a prospective pregnancy exposure registry, preferably a disease-based multiproduct pregnancy registry, using a cohort analysis that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to etrasimod regardless of indication during pregnancy with unexposed comparator population(s) in a timely manner. Align the study protocol with protocol(s) outside the US to reach the target sample size. The registry will identify and record pregnancy complications, major and minor congenital malformations, spontaneous abortion, stillbirths, elective terminations, preterm births, small-for-gestational-age births, and any other adverse outcomes, including postnatal growth and development. Outcomes described in the protocol will be assessed throughout pregnancy. Infant outcomes, including effects on postnatal growth and development, will be assessed through at least the first year of life.

requirement.text: 4499-5 Conduct an additional pregnancy study that uses a different design from the prospective pregnancy registry established to fulfill postmarketing requirement 4499-4 (for example a retrospective cohort study using claims or electronic medical record data or a case-control study) to assess major congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, small for gestational age births, and preterm births in women exposed to etrasimod regardless of indication during pregnancy compared to an unexposed control population.
